[PhD Candidate in Economics · University of Manitoba]{.eyebrow}

# I study how wildfire smoke, land and water shape Canadian agriculture.

::: {.lead}
My research is in environmental, resource and agricultural economics, with a focus on wildfire and air quality, land and water conservation, and applied econometrics for policy evaluation. Through WWGD Research & Consulting, I bring the same methods to private-sector problems.
:::

[Academic research]{.eyebrow}

### Wildfire, farmland and conservation

A dissertation on the economic effects of wildfire smoke on Canadian agriculture, a working paper on wildfire exposure and farmland values, and published work on the costs and benefits of wetland retention in Manitoba.

[Papers and publications →](research.qmd)

[WWGD Research & Consulting]{.eyebrow}

### Research-grade analysis for business

Econometrics, machine learning, strategy and competitive intelligence for organizations, from predictive driver-safety models to fuel-purchase compliance audits for a Canadian freight carrier.

[Current thesis work]{.eyebrow}

## Wildfire Smoke and Canadian Crop Production

What is the net effect of wildfire smoke on crop production in Canada? Using a 2006–2023 crop-by-region panel and wind-driven variation in smoke from distant fires.
